text:
len: Quick thread 1: need clarity on billing unit for Performance Lane pilot. Two options on the table: 'concurrency-minutes' (engineering preferred) vs. 'requests' (sales/customer language). We must pick one for pilot docs and UI.

oscar: Field feedback: customers buy in requests / calls. They get confused by "concurrency". Keep buyer-facing unit simple.

mei: Eng constraints: enforcing per-request billing is tricky for long-running requests and streaming. Concurrency-minutes maps directly to slots and is cheaper to implement. One credit = 1 concurrent request for 60s makes enforcement easier.

pricing-bot: Scan note: conversion examples strongly recommended in pricing docs. Recommend publishing an equivalence table: e.g., typical request durations -> requests-per-credit. Logged ticket PR-2041.

len: We need a UX compromise: show buyers requests-equivalent on UI but bill by concurrency-minutes under the hood. Example: show "1 Burst Credit = ~10 short requests (100ms)" with a tooltip linking to full calcs.

oscar: +1 for that. Sales wants the console to show "estimated API-calls remaining" so non-technical purchasers feel comfortable.

mei: Implementation note: we'll need a small runtime hook that tracks median request duration per route (rolling 1h) for conversion. Use that to compute display-estimate. Actual billing will use exact concurrency-minute usage.

cs-lead: CSM ask: include real worked examples in buyer kit: realtime chat app (50ms calls), doc summarization (1.2s calls), batch rerank (10s calls). For each, show cost of 1k requests using burst-packs.

legal: Contract note: must clearly state "displayed estimates are for planning only; billing is based on measured concurrency-minute usage." Add a one-liner in T&Cs.

len: Example draft UI copy for review: "Burst Packs are consumed based on concurrent request time (1 credit = 60s at one concurrent request). The console displays estimated API-call equivalents for planning; actual consumption is measured and billed precisely." Thoughts?

oscar: tweak: change "consumed based on concurrent request time" -> "consumed based on concurrent request time (concurrency-minutes)" to teach term. But keep tooltip for non-technical.

mei: Technical follow-ups: 1) add per-route rolling median duration metric; 2) expose estimate API to UI; 3) ensure billing pipeline accepts sub-minute prorating. Can do in next sprint but need spec.

pricing-bot: Suggested pack sizes: Starter (10k credits), Business (50k), Scale (250k). Example pricing rows attached in PR-2041. Surge top-ups: 3x base unit.

cs-lead: Pilot requirements: 1) Buyer kit with 3 worked examples, 2) console mock showing estimated API-call equivalents and remaining balance, 3) CSM playbook for entitlement and manual purchase flow.

len: Launch gates proposal: a) telemetry for conversion accuracy (error <20% over 24h); b) billing QA w/ synthetic traffic; c) legal T&C snippet; d) two pilot customers using different workload patterns.

oscar: Ops ask: add alert when estimated-equivalent deviates >25% from observed request counts for 30m. Helps detect mismatches.

mei: Will prototype UI hook and estimate API. Also will add sim-mode in QA to exercise throttling and credit consumption.

legal: Draft T&C snippet: "Displayed API-call equivalents are estimates for planning; actual consumption and billing are calculated from measured concurrency-minute usage." Will add to pilot T&Cs.

len: Action items (due Thu EOD): pricing-bot finalize pack sizes & price table, mei spec estimate API + QA sim-mode, legal drop T&C into pilot SOW, cs-lead assemble buyer kit examples. We'll pick final unit language for customer docs Monday.

posscript: pricing-bot created PR-2041 and linked a sample spreadsheet. I'll schedule a short follow-up Fri 9am PT to review UI mock. Thanks all :rocket:
